bees — dance angle and duration encode direction and distance relative to the sun

beetles — celestial polarization and brightness cues stabilize navigation away from competitors

moths — background matching changes visual detection probability rather than making an animal invisible
butterflies — programmed tissue remodeling and imaginal development construct adult organs

termites — mound geometry couples wind and thermal buoyancy to gas exchange

spiders — high-speed web deformation with strand-force and capture-success measurements
spiders — controlled visual stimuli with eye-field occlusion and three-dimensional movement tracking
scorpions — controlled vibration sources with sensory occlusion and orientation measurements
scorpions — high-speed strike records and non-instructional venom-volume assays linked to prey restraint
mantises — high-speed joint kinematics with strike distance and capture-success measurements
mantises — tracked sway under varied wind with calibrated predator-detection trials

exclusions: Use precise entomology and arachnology; spiders and scorpions are arachnids, not insects.
Avoid fear bait, disgust bait, invented motives, and claims that colony behavior requires a central commander.
Do not provide actionable venom extraction, pest-harm, or unsafe handling instructions.
Distinguish observed behavior from inference and avoid describing every interaction as aggression.
prompt_context: Use precise entomology and arachnology. Build each episode around one legacy subject, observable structure or behavior, bounded habitat interval, biological mechanism, and named evidence method. Avoid fear bait and invented motives; visceral details may appear only when they clarify the real lifecycle or mechanism.
